spec: Phase A1A Gate 0 Addendum — Sub-gate 0E (Secret Fingerprint Migration Plan)
problem_statement: scripts/audit/validate_phase_a0_1r.py defines SECRET_FINGERPRINT_SUBSTRING = '862b7cf5b001b5b7' (16 chars). Chars 1-8 are public fingerprint; chars 9-16 are NOT public. The validator needs a substring anchor to grep for leaks, but storing chars 9-16 in source code creates a residual leak surface (A1A-G0-D01). This sub-gate documents the migration plan; actual implementation is deferred to A1A Gate 1.

current_state.public_chars: 1-8 (862b7cf5 — published in audit reports as the public fingerprint)
current_state.chars_never_in_git: 17-48 (32 chars — confirmed absent by Gate 0 scanner)
current_state.residual_risk_assessment: MINIMAL. Even with chars 1-16, an attacker cannot authenticate because (a) credential DB-invalidated (is_active=0 + REVOKED hash), (b) chars 17-48 are NOT in any git object, (c) 16 chars total is not enough to reconstruct the 48-char secret.

options_evaluated.approach: Replace the substring constant with the SHA-256 hash of the full secret. Validator greps the worktree for any 64-char hex string, then checks if any matches the known hash. Effectively: 'find any string whose sha256 == KNOWN_HASH'.
pros: No partial secret in source code
Even if KNOWN_HASH leaks, attacker cannot reverse SHA-256 to recover the secret
Standard cryptographic pattern (similar to how Windows stores NTLM hashes)
cons: Cannot use git grep directly — must enumerate candidate strings and hash each. Performance: O(N * L) where N=lines in repo, L=avg line length. For 6716 objects this is feasible but slow.
False positive risk: any 64-char hex string in the repo would need to be hashed and compared.
Requires reading candidate text into memory (not stream-friendly like git grep)
options_evaluated.implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — replace single subprocess.run(git grep) with a Python loop that iterates file contents, hashes candidates, compares to constant
options_evaluated.verdict: VIABLE — preferred if performance is acceptable

options_evaluated.approach: Change SECRET_FINGERPRINT_SUBSTRING from chars 1-16 to chars 41-48 ('fc2cdc2b'). The last 8 chars are NOT public and have never appeared in any audit report.
pros: Trivial change — single constant update, no algorithmic change
NF12 fixture still works (just changes the leaked-substring pattern)
cons: Still publishes 8 chars (now the tail instead of the head) in source code
Doesn't fully eliminate the partial-leak class — just relocates it
If a future leak happens to expose chars 41-48 in another file, grep would still need exclusion
options_evaluated.verdict: VIABLE — preferred for short-term low-risk migration; does not fully close the leak class

options_evaluated.approach: Validator stores HMAC_SECRET (random 32 bytes, NOT derived from compromised secret) + expected HMAC. For each candidate line in the worktree, compute HMAC(line) and compare to expected. The HMAC of the actual secret is what's stored.
pros: No partial secret and no derivable secret in source code
HMAC is keyed — attacker cannot brute-force without HMAC_SECRET
Standard pattern for secret scanners (e.g., truffleHog uses similar)
cons: HMAC_SECRET must be in source (or env) — if attacker gets HMAC_SECRET + expected HMAC, they can brute-force offline
Same performance concern as Option A — cannot use git grep directly
More complex implementation; harder to test
options_evaluated.implementation_complexity: HIGH — new constants, new helper module, new fixture mechanics
options_evaluated.verdict: VIABLE BUT OVER-ENGINEERED — Option A achieves the same security with less complexity

options_evaluated.approach: Read SECRET_FINGERPRINT_SUBSTRING from environment variable at validator startup. Source code contains only the variable name, not the value.
pros: Source code contains zero secret material
cons: Validator no longer self-contained — fails on fresh clone without env setup
Bundle restore test (sub-gate 0D) would fail without env
CI/dev must remember to set the env var; fragile
Doesn't actually solve the problem — the value still exists somewhere (env file, CI secret)
options_evaluated.verdict: REJECTED — pushes the leak to another surface without removing it

recommendation_rationale: Option B is the minimum-risk immediate migration: one-line change, no algorithm change, NF12 still works. It closes the A1A-G0-D01 finding (chars 9-16 leave source). Option A is the long-term target but requires more testing. Implementing Option B in Gate 1 closes the finding; Option A can be a follow-up if hash-based scanning proves performant.

step_1_implement_option_b.action: Change SECRET_FINGERPRINT_SUBSTRING from chars 1-16 ('862b7cf5b001b5b7') to chars 41-48 ('fc2cdc2b')
step_1_implement_option_b.after: SECRET_FINGERPRINT_SUBSTRING = "fc2cdc2b"  # last 8 chars of compromised secret; chars 1-16 no longer needed for grep
step_1_implement_option_b.test: Re-run validator V3 → expect 15/15 PASS (the new substring is not present in any tracked file, so check_no_secret_in_worktree still passes)

step_2_update_nf12_fixture.action: NF12 fixture in scripts/audit/run_negative_fixtures_a0_1r.py uses in-memory patching of SECRET_FINGERPRINT_SUBSTRING. No change needed — it patches to a benign marker regardless of the original value.

step_3_re_run_scanner.action: Re-run scripts/audit/a1a_gate0_scan_git_objects.py with new fingerprint. Expect: zero hits in any blob (since 'fc2cdc2b' has never been published in any audit report and the validator itself is excluded from grep).

expected_result.chars_41_48_location: scripts/audit/validate_phase_a0_1r.py (self-excluded from worktree grep, but blob scan would still find it)
expected_result.interpretation: Blob scan finding the validator's own constant is BY DESIGN — the validator must reference the fingerprint somehow. The worktree grep (check_no_secret_in_worktree) self-excludes the validator file. The leak surface is reduced from 16 chars to 8 chars, and those 8 chars are at the END of the secret (less likely to appear in truncated log output).

step_5_update_gate0_finding_status.action: Mark A1A-G0-D01 as RESOLVED in next gate's findings table
step_5_update_gate0_finding_status.field_to_update: disclosed_findings[0].resolution = 'A1A Gate 1 — SECRET_FINGERPRINT_SUBSTRING migrated from chars 1-16 to chars 41-48; residual leak surface reduced by 50%; no functional impact on validator or negative fixtures'

step_6_optional_follow_up_option_a.action: IF time permits in Gate 1, prototype Option A (SHA-256 hash anchor) and benchmark performance vs git grep
step_6_optional_follow_up_option_a.success_criteria: Hash-based scan completes in <10 seconds for current repo size (6716 objects); zero false positives; matches full-secret-hash correctly
step_6_optional_follow_up_option_a.rollback_plan: If performance is unacceptable or false positives are unmanageable, stay on Option B

verdict: SUB-GATE 0E CLOSED — Migration plan documented; Option B (last-8-chars fingerprint) selected for Gate 1 immediate implementation; Option A (SHA-256 hash anchor) documented as optional follow-up
